#2134. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 13 novembre

Endrick ma non solo. La Roma tiene molti tavoli aperti per gennaio anche se il brasiliano rimane chiaramente il principale obiettivo. I giallorossi ci lavorano da questa estate e nonostante il Real Madrid continui a ribadire che non partirà nella sessione invernale, i segnali di radiomercato vanno in un’altra direzione. Ed è per questo che il direttore sportivo Tony D’Amico tiene vivi i contatti con l’entourage del giocatore. L’operazione sarebbe molto costosa ma la Roma ha messo in preventivo anche questo, sapendo che il suo arrivo potrebbe dare la spinta decisiva per lottare fino in fondo per lo scudetto. Esistono però le alternative e allora facciamo il punto della situazione. L’ultimo nome che è entrato nell’agenda è Keny Arroyo, esterno offensivo ecuadoriano, classe 2006, attualmente in forza al Cruzeiro, che nel 2025 lo ha acquistato dal Besiktas. Ha un contratto fino al 31 dicembre 2029, una clausola rescissoria altissima ma con un’offerta da 45 milioni potrebbe anche partire. Un altro profilo che piace e non poco è l’ex Atletico Madrid Samuel Lino, che gioca nel Flamengo. Anche questa un’operazione molto costosa. La Roma stava pensando ad un’offerta da 25 milioni di euro ma il club brasiliano su queste basi non intende trattare. Ovviamente tra i profili monitorati rimane Kvernadze del Frosinone protagonista di un grande avvio di stagione. Nel suo contratto c’è una clausola di rescissione di 4 milioni valida per l’estate. La Roma però ha bisogno subito di un rinforzo e quindi sta valutando se fare una proposta impossibile da rifiutare alla società gialloblù,. Gittens del Chelsea resta tra i preferiti ma le riflessioni riguardano anche le sue condizioni fisiche. Sempre da tenere presente anche Lewelling dello Stoccarda, che i giallorossi aveva quasi preso nell’ultimo giorno del mercato estivo.

L'Inter sta monitorando diversi giovani calciatori per il futuro. Uno di questi è Jay Robinson, attaccante del Monza che sta facendo molto bene nel suo primo spezzone di Serie A. È in prestito - secco - dal Southampton e ha una valutazione intorno ai dieci milioni di euro. Non è escluso che ci possa essere l'intenzione di sopravanzare i concorrenti cercando di trovare un accordo con il club inglese, salvo poi lasciarlo ancora in prestito per qualche mese, fino alla scadenza del prestito, in Brianza. Nei giorni scorsi intanto ci sono stati contatti preliminari fra l'Inter e Alessandro Bastoni per il possibile rinnovo contrattuale. Il difensore centrale ha ventisette anni e può essere a uno degli ultimi contratti della carriera - forse non è ancora l'ultimo - dunque non ha intenzione di recedere dalla sua posizione contrattuale attuale, intorno ai 6 milioni di euro, anzi. L'accordo contrattuale che vige in questo momento non è poi molto lungo, anzi. Perché a gennaio ci sarà solamente un anno e mezzo per regolamentare la situazione, anche se Bastoni negli ultimi anni ha sempre detto di volere rimanere all'Inter e diventare una bandiera, anche quando c'erano squadre importanti come il Bayern Monaco a chiedere quale fosse la sua situazione. È evidente quindi che la volontà non sia cambiata e che non ci sia l'intenzione di cambiare a ogni costo, ma servirà una proposta all'altezza. Se è vero che sono stati prospettati interessamenti, dall'altro lato non ci sono ancora colloqui intercorsi con squadre che potrebbero essere protagoniste nel prossimo futuro, come il Barcellona. È chiaro che più ci si avvicina alla scadenza, più il coltello dalla parte del manico è per il calciatore, comunque richiestissimo dalle big negli scorsi anni.

Riflessioni in corso in casa del Torino su Gvidas Gineitis. Il centrocampista in estate è stato ad un passo dal lasciare i granata per accasarsi al Celtic, che ha presentato due offerte differenti al Toro. Entrambe però sono state ritenute insufficienti dal club. Ci sarà un ritorno del club scozzese in inverno? Possibile, ma al momento il giocatore sembra essere rimasto leggermente scottato da quanto accaduto in estate. Nonostante il tecnico del Celtic Martin O'Neill caldeggiasse il suo arrivo, dal lato societario (del Celtic) non hanno fatto uno sforzo per venire incontro al Torino per colmare il non impossibile gap economico. Insomma, è sembrato che il club non lo volesse per davvero. Nel frattempo Gineitis è diventato importante anche per Ignazio Abate, che difficilmente fa a meno di lui. Fra il Torino e l'entourage del giocatore ci sono stati i primi contatti per parlare del da farsi nel prossimo mercato. Il lituano ha rinnovato l'ultima volta un anno fa, legandosi al club fino al 2029 con opzione per una ulteriore stagione. Possibile comunque che per una offerta di circa 8-10 milioni il Torino lo lasci partire. Da capire se, in caso di effettivo ritorno da parte del Celtic con una simile somma, il giocatore possa essere ancora convinto dall'unirsi alla squadra scozzese. E se, nel frattempo, altre squadre si faranno avanti per lui.

La Juventus si è inserita con decisione nella corsa per Gustavo Varela. I bianconeri vogliono dire la loro per il giovane attaccante portoghese del Monza che piace anche al Napoli e a diversi top club europei come Arsenal, Tottenham e Barcellona. L'operazione per gennaio appare complessa poiché il club brianzolo intende trattenerlo per la salvezza e valuta il cartellino tra i 30 e i 35 milioni di euro in vista della sessione estiva. Il fattore chiave per il futuro del giocatore sarà la qualità del progetto sportivo proposto. Nel frattempo, l'attaccante resta concentrato unicamente sul Monza e sulla Nazionale portoghese.

"Con Kvernadze ci stiamo lavorando, succede con i rinnovi e le clausole e sono fiduciose che possiamo mettere le cose a posto. Può avere un futuro di buon livello, deve migliorare, ma fisicamente è un top". Renzo Castagnini, direttore sportivo del Frosinone, al Forum di redazione di TuttoMercatoWeb (che potete trovare qui in versione integrale) ha spiegato qual è la situazione di Giorgi Kvernadze, attaccante georgiano che ha avuto un impatto straordinario con la Serie A. Il Frosinone ha intenzione di prolungargli l'accordo, ritoccandolo verso l'alto. Normale dopo le ottime prestazioni in questo principio di stagione, anche perché per ora guadagna 200 mila euro, un'inezia per un club di Serie A. Così la proposta per il prolungamento può toccare il milione di euro all'anno, per solleticarne il palato ed evitare uno scippo che potrebbe arrivare, ma non a gennaio. In questo momento all'interno del contratto di Kvernadze c'è una clausola risolutoria da 4 milioni di euro. Bassissima, ma che può essere attivata solamente a giugno. C'è tempo dunque per cercare un prolungamento che cancelli questa possibilità, lasciando al Frosinone più agio dal punto di vista delle trattative. Resta da capire se pure il calciatore sia d'accordo.

Il Parma ha rinnovato il contratto di Dominik Drobnic, centrale sloveno classe 2007 che è diventato rapidamente una risorsa importante per Cuesta e Gilardino: "Ci sono percorsi che raccontano più di una semplice crescita sportiva. Quello di Dominik Drobnič con il Parma è uno di questi. Arrivato nel 2023 dal NK Bravo, il difensore sloveno ha compiuto passo dopo passo il proprio percorso in gialloblu, dall'Under 17 alla Primavera, fino a conquistare un posto nella rosa della Prima Squadra. Un cammino impreziosito, nella scorsa stagione sportiva, dalla finale del Campionato Primavera 1 e dal riconoscimento individuale come miglior difensore della stagione. Oggi questo percorso si lega ancora più fortemente al futuro: Parma Calcio 1913 è lieto infatti di annunciare il rinnovo del contratto di Dominik Drobnič sino al 30 giugno 2030. Classe 2007, mancino, Drobnič ha già assaporato il calcio dei grandi, debuttando in Serie A nello scorso mese di agosto. Sono finora sei le presenze nella massima serie, a cui si aggiunge quella in Coppa Italia. Una firma che racchiude il valore del tempo, del lavoro e della fiducia. Perché dietro ogni giovane talento c'è un percorso da accompagnare e una storia da raccontare. Il Parma sceglie di continuare a scriverla insieme a Dominik, confermando la propria attenzione verso i giovani e la volontà di investire su chi, giorno dopo giorno, scegliere di voler crescere con i colori e i valori del Parma addosso".

Mauricio Pochettino è ufficialmente il nuovo allenatore del Manchester United. Il tecnico argentino ha firmato fino all'estate del 2029 ed entrerà in carica ufficialmente dal 18 novembre per succedere a Michael Carrick. È arrivato anche l'annuncio da parte del club inglese con tutti i dettagli, dopo la firma arrivata nelle scorse ore: "Mauricio Pochettino ha accettato di diventare il nuovo allenatore della prima squadra maschile del Manchester United a partire dal 18 novembre. Il club ha raggiunto un accordo con la Federcalcio statunitense (U.S. Soccer Federation) affinché Mauricio e il suo staff vengano liberati al termine dei loro impegni con la Nazionale maschile degli Stati Uniti".

Restando in casa Red Devils, il futuro di Bruno Fernandes al Manchester United appare sempre più incerto. Il portoghese ha rifiutato una seconda offerta di rinnovo contrattuale proposta dalla società, con il suo attuale accordo in scadenza al termine della stagione in corso, quindi al 30 giugno 2026. Il 32enne aveva già respinto una prima proposta formulata durante la scorsa estate, momento in cui erano stati avviati i colloqui tra le parti. Nonostante i due rifiuti consecutivi, la dirigenza del Manchester United non intende interrompere i negoziati e mantiene l'obiettivo di trattenere il giocatore. Il club inglese dispone comunque di un'opzione che gli permette di estendere unilateralmente il contratto per un'ulteriore stagione, una clausola che impedirebbe a Bruno Fernandes di trattare liberamente con altri club esteri a partire dal mese di gennaio per un eventuale trasferimento a parametro zero.

L'Athletic Club ha annunciato di aver prolungato il contratto di un giovane talento del vivaio che ha già fatto capolino in prima squadra nella passata stagione. Si tratta del fantasista classe 2006 Adrian Perez. In Francia, invece, il Lens ha ufficializzato la nomina di Didier Digard come nuovo allenatore della prima squadra. Il tecnico francese ha firmato un contratto fino a giugno 2028 e raccoglie l'eredità di Yannick Cahuzac alla guida dei Sang et Or. La società ha spiegato di aver seguito il consueto processo decisionale, coordinato dal presidente Joseph Oughourlian, valutando diversi candidati (Sage e Regragui su tutti) prima di individuare in Digard il profilo ideale. Il Lens ha sottolineato come la scelta sia maturata attraverso un'attenta analisi interna, al di là delle indiscrezioni circolate negli ultimi giorni.

#2133. Inside the insane trophy room of Chelsea legend Branislav Ivanovic: Framed pictures of his 42 goals, a ring from Didier Drogba... and an LED football pitch

Published: 04:50 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 12:08 EST, 8 November 2026

Legendary Chelsea defender Branislav Ivanovic's insane private trophy room has gone viral after a fan posted a tour of the museum online.

The now 42-year-old made 377 appearances for the Blues during a nine-year stint at the club from 2008 to 2017.

He enjoyed a hugely successful time with the west London side, winning ten trophies and becoming one of the club's most decorated defenders.

As well as winning three Premier League titles he landed three FA Cups,  the League Cup, the Community Shield and the Europa League. He also has a Champions League winners' medal with the Blues, though the Serb did miss out on playing in the 2012 final after famously being told by Geoff Shreeves live on Sky Sports that he was suspended following their win over Barcelona in the semi-final.

Branislav Ivanovic won 10 trophies with Chelsea across nine years with the Blues

The Chelsea legend has built a private trophy room in his hometown of Sremska Mitrovica to rival any other

In a video posted to Instagram a fan from Ivanovic's hometown Sremska Mitrovica explained he was allowed access to the private showroom and documented the breadth of trophies, personal honours and shirts he has collected throughout his illustrious career.

Many of the souvenirs are from his time in Russia with Lokomotiv Moscow and Zenit St Petersburg, as well as those he got at Chelsea.

The private museum holds over hundreds of shirts alone and has an entire wall adorned with shirts just given to him and signed by someone he either played with or played against including the likes of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Neymar and Javier Zanetti.

Most Chelsea fans will remember Ivanovic's most crucial goals such as his winners in the Champions League round of 16 against Napoli and the 2013 Europa League final against Benfica.

And the Serbian appears to have made an effort to immortalise every single one of his club goals by framing and displaying a photo of all 42 from throughout his career.

Amongst other quirky designs, the room has a set of football leg stools for guests to sit on at the bar

Mourinho gets a mention having won the Premier League, Fa Cup and League cup with the Serbian in the 2014-15 season

There is also a replica of every trophy he has won in his career as well and a specialty ring he received as a gift from Didier Drogba after Chelsea's 2012 Champions League triumph.

Ivanovic didn't forget to add some style to the room by installing an LED football pitch to light the room and putting swanky football leg chairs at a fully stocked bar.

He even has a slide solely dedicated to displaying quotes from his former manager Jose Mourinho including the Special One's description of Ivanovic as 'The Perfect One'.

Since leaving Chelsea in 2017 the Serb moved back to Zenit St Petersburg before ending his career back in England with West Brom in 2021.

#2132. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

The hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

Martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

#2131. Sheffield United summer signing scores in 4-0 win on international captaincy debut

Bangladesh ran out as 4-0 winners over Sri Lanka to progress to the semi-finals of the SAFF Championship, where they will lock horns with Pakistan. After Shamit Shome broke the deadlock inside nine minutes, Sheffield United man Hamza Choudhury was on hand to double the lead.

The SUFC man ventured forward with a darting run in behind the defence before emphatically slotting home.

Further goals from Boreham Wood’s Farhaan Ali Wahid – currently on loan from Fulham – and Rakib Hossain put the finishing touches on a convincing victory in the second half. It made it back-to-back victories for Bangladesh for the first time since 2023.

A former England U21s international, Choudhury stepped in to lead the team for the first time in the absence of long-serving captain Jamal Bhuyan.

Ex-Leicester City and Watford man Choudhury changed allegiance from England to Bangladesh in December of 2024, a move which is beginning to pay dividends.

His debut came in March last year against India, before netting his first goal in a 2-0 win over Bhutan just over two months later. Choudhury now adds another feather to his international cap by captaining his country for the first time.

Switching allegiance to Bangladesh marked a significant turning point for the South Asian nation, with Choudhury becoming their first player to play in the Premier League. He has been hailed as the figurehead to drive forward a country not renowned for its football exploits.

After a damaging 9-2 defeat to Indonesia, which saw them crash out of the FIFA ASEAN Cup in the last international break, Choudhury’s side have bounced back in perfect fashion and he has been at the heart of that.

Deployed in both his conventional midfield role as well as at right-back, the former Burton Albion loanee will be pivotal if they are to end their 23-year wait for an international title in the SAFF Championship.

While his form on the international stage has gone to another level, Choudhury has lacked consistency at Sheffield United this term.

The 29-year-old put pen to paper on a permanent deal at Bramall Lane following a successful loan stint and has been a mainstay at right-back after Femi Seriki was ruled out for the season with a patellar tendon rupture.

He produced impressive displays in their three-game unbeaten run, victories over Preston North End and Wrexham and a draw with Derby County, but he was taken off at half-time in their latest defeat to Charlton Athletic.

Given Seriki’s absence, Choudhury will be keen to regain his best form and will need to do so if SUFC are to enter the Championship play-off conversation, with his recent exploits for Bangladesh potentially providing the confidence to reignite his season.

#2129. Sebastiano Esposito, l’agente: “Ora non pensa al mercato, ma potrebbe giocare benissimo in un tridente con Hojlund e Vergara”

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio, è intervenuto l’agente Mario Giuffredi: “Io vivo le partite dei miei assistiti con grande passione e coinvolgimento. Come se fossi con loro in campo. Durante la partita non riesco a essere distaccato, sono molto acceso. Dopo la partita, ritorna l’equilibrio. E riesco anche a essere più equilibrato delle critiche degli stessi calciatori. Come ho vissuto i due rigori degli Esposito? Non ho visto nessuno dei due rigori di Pio e Sebastiano. Ero anche a cena con Salvatore Esposito. Capivamo in base alle reazioni degli altri che erano con noi a tavola. Pio sentiva la responsabilità della partita. Aver segnato quel rigore contro la Francia toglieva il pensiero del rigore della Bosnia. Pio ha una lunga carriera, può migliorare statistiche con Nazionale e club. Io non guardo le pagelle, so come ragionano i giornalisti, che non si limitano a guardare la prestazione, ma anche episodi, dettagli. La prestazione di Sebastiano è stata saggia a livello tattico. Ha giocato in posizioni di campo non suoi. Mi dispiace che i giornalisti non si limitano a questo, ma si limitano a guardare il rigore sbagliato. Per sbagliare quel rigore, devi avere il coraggio di batterlo. Sull’1-1, contro quel portiere (Maignan ndr) e contro quella Nazionale, devi avere coraggio. Io mi ero arrabbiato con Sebastiano se non avesse avuto il coraggio di andare dal disco. Sebastiano Esposito e Vergara insieme con Hojlund? Si incastrerebbero benissimo, perché Sebastiano è un toro a livello fisico. Vergara ha grande forza nelle gambe. Hanno anche colpi tecnici, sono imprevedibili. Non sarebbe maschio. Però non facciamo i direttori del Napoli né gli allenatori del Napoli. Aiutare il Napoli portando Sebastiano Esposito? Io non mi sono mai sottratto ad aiutare il Napoli e mai lo farò. Al tempo stesso non sono io che vado a insistere per far prendere quel tipo di giocatore. Sono orgoglioso di quello che sono. Il fatto di essere arrivato dalla galetta mi rende orgoglioso. Negli ultimi due anni ho avuto la media di quattro giocatori convocati in Nazionale. Vedo che nel primo e nel secondo tempo ho due giocatori su tre in campo. Ieri sera dopo la partita, presa coscienza, ho preso l’auto e sono andato nei luoghi dove tutto è iniziato. Per un napoletano è tutto più difficile, ci sono tantissimi ostacoli messi davanti da invidiosi. Hai sentito Pio Esposito dopo la partita contro la Francia? Il futuro di Pio è all’Inter, senza dubbio. Sta benissimo. Il club ha mostrato sempre attacco e riconoscenza. Sebastiano si trova benissimo al Sassuolo, in questo momento non pensare neanche al mercato. Quello che succederà si vedrà. Entrambi stanno bene dove stanno. Pio sicuramente rimarrà all’Inter per tanti anni, è la sua seconda pelle; mentre Sebastiano magari si vedrà strada facendo se sia meritevole di alzare ancora di più il livello, ma è prematuro parlare di mercato.Il paragone di Pio Esposito con Meazza? Noi vediamo tutto con serenità ed equilibrio. Io vivo con questa concezione: ci addormentiamo la sera con la consapevolezza che il mattino possa finire tutto. Questo ci permette di non cullarci su certe cose. Il calcio è lo sport più bello e più crudo del mondo. Uno dei più grandi giocatori per me è stato Roberto Baggio. Lui a tratti viene dimenticato, nessuno gli ha dato un posto di un certo livello. Il calcio ha bisogno di gente come Roberto Baggio. Questo mi fa pensare che un giocatore verrà dimenticato in un secondo. Perciò bisogna vivere tutto con equilibrio. Qual è il prossimo che la mia scuderia ha in rampa di lancio? Te ne dico due. Quando dico le cose ci metto la faccia e vado anche controcorrente. Dico Favasuli e Marianucci. Per me Marianucci può arrivare in Nazionale, è un difensore di grandissimo livello. Ha qualcosa in più rispetto a tanti altri. Se migliora nell’attenzione, diventa di grande livello. Favasuli lo diamo per scontato, perché è partito bene”.

#2128. ‘Definitely’: Birmingham City reporter delivers Chris Davies contract verdict amid impressive turnaround

Birmingham City have won six of their last seven Championship games to surge to the top of the table after 15 matches. BCFC are in a fine position as the November international break continues, and the work of Chris Davies has drawn significant praise.

There have been doubts over his Blues future at times, especially during a disappointing 2025/26 season, but Davies has completed an impressive turnaround to secure his position. And, one man who believes the Welshman’s work should be rewarded with a new deal is Birmingham Live’s Alex Dicken.

When quizzed on Davies’ contract situation in a fan Q&A, Blues reporter Dicken wrote: “I think they should give it a few months to allow the relationship between John Murtough (Birmingham City’s new director of football) and Davies to develop – and get the transfer window done and dusted – but it’s definitely something that should be looked at before the end of the season.

“I think Chris Davies is the sort of manager who will want security and to know where he stands. It is remarkable what he’s done in the last six months when you consider he faced questions over his future at the club in March/April last year. He has shown huge development as a young manager.”

Davies started strongly as he led a strong Birmingham City side to a rampant League One title win. That was expected though, so the boss and his side rose to the Championship with a point to prove.

And, they failed to prove it. Last season, BCFC struggled for consistency and frustrated their supporters with football that was often drab and unimaginative. It led to calls for Davies to be replaced by a bigger name, but the hierarchy stuck by their boss.

There were some lingering doubts early this season, but the doubters have been silenced with a stunning surge to the summit of the Championship. Birmingham City play with much more speed and impetus in possession, as shown by the fact that they have scored 21 goals in the last 10 games. They’ve maintained defensive solidity too though, with Christoph Klarer and Phil Neumann starring.

Davies was criticised for not adapting or getting the best out of City’s attacking talents last season. He has done both of those things this term though, highlighting his own development and growth as a boss.

Davies dealt with the pressure of turning around Birmingham City’s fortunes. But, such is the ambition of the club that he must now take on the task of maintaining their impressive form.

BCFC have eyes on a rise to the Premier League with a new stadium on the horizon and dreams of a Jude Bellingham return remaining for Tom Wagner.

Davies’ importance in this cannot be overstated, and further security over his future would be richly deserved. His current contract runs until 2028, so entrusting him with the next stage of their project means a new contract will be required.

As Dicken argues though, perhaps it is best to wait until new director of football Murtough is settled. If a relationship can be built between the two, an agreement becomes even more logical.

#2127. To infinity and beyond! Another stunning Diego Gomez strike has Brighton up to SECOND and daring to dream... as Brentford's Igor Thiago is goaded into a red card

Published: 11:08 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 12:40 EST, 8 November 2026

Onwards and upwards go Brighton. Another victory to send them soaring into second place with only Arsenal above them.

It is a lofty perch for the Seagulls and one more admirable when considering the depths from which they have risen.

Homeless and penniless, on the brink of extinction at the end of the last century they are now daring to dream about the Champions League.

To infinity and beyond. Why not? Fabian Hurzeler’s team have already beaten Arsenal and Manchester City without conceding this season.

The only goals scored against them in the last six Premier League games came at Liverpool, where they lost 2-0 but were not outplayed.

City’s season is mired in uncertainty, awaiting sentence for financial breaches and the other half of the traditional Big Six are so erratic there will likely be scope for interlopers when the prized European tickets are handed out in May.

It is six months away but at this moment in time there are not four teams better than Fabian Hurzeler’s.

Brighton appear fully formed. Delightfully fluent in attack. Creative with zip and imagination and different ways to score goals.

There is a defined style of play. Solid at the back with enough sporting maturity to survive a test of needle, which this became against Brentford after the red card for Igor Thiago’s red card.

Diego Gomez celebrated another memorable strike at the Amex Stadium after his halfway-line stunner in the 5-0 win over Crystal Palace

The Bees already trailed to a screamer from the left boot of Diego Gomez and went further behind before half time when Pascal Gross converted a penalty awarded for a shirt pull by Keane Lewis-Potter on Luka Vuskovic.

Brighton (4-2-3-1): Verbruggen 6; Costinha 6, Dunk 6, Vuskovic 6, Boscagli 7; Gross 8, Andres 6 (Wieffer 46, ); Gomez 7 (Yalcoue 90+3), Ayari 7 (Hinshelwood 78), De Cuyper 7 (Minteh 82); Kostoulas 6 (Rutter 82)

Subs not used: Steele, Hadjam, Kadioglu, Svoboda

Bookings: Andres, Boscagli, Wieffer, Dunk

Brentford (4-3-3): Kelleher 6; Kayode 5, Ajer 6, Van den Berg 6 (Wilson 70), Lewis-Potter 5 (Diouf 59); Sangare 5 (Jensen 59), Janelt 5, Hickey 5 (Collins 46); Ouattara 4 (Yarmoliuk 46), Thiago 3, Schade 4

Subs not used: Valdimarsson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster

Gross, the 35-year-old midfielder schemer who walloped his penalty into the top corner in emphatic fashion, embodies the confidence pulsing through this team and his goal closed the contest.

The Bees assembled in the deep looking to minimise damage with an eye on a counterattack or a set piece and maybe hoping the officials would see fit to even it up at 10 against 10.

It didn’t happen. Instead, Brighton controlled the ball. They have had more than 75 per cent of possession across 90 minutes and spent the second half probing around the fringes of the Brentford penalty area.

They registered 20 shots in all but there would be no third goal. And nobody minded. They celebrated the victory and a return to the Amex Stadium after five away games in a row and more than 5,000 miles on the road.

Every substitution made by Hurzeler came as a reminder of their strength and quality.

Kaoru Mitoma, yet to feature this season, is expected back from injury soon after the international break.

The Conference League is not proving a distraction to a squad of such depth and Hurzeler gave fans his permission to dream.

'They should be always excited,' said the Brighton boss. 'That’s our job. They can dream. They can have high expectations, but these are things we can’t control. We played good game but always things we can do better.'

This was Brentford’s second defeat in this Premier League season and they had players sent off in both.

'In both scenarios the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation, antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way,' fumed boss Keith Andrews, referring to Yehor Yarmoliuk’s red card against Liverpool, when the Bees finished the game with nine men.

'We should do better, but the game is in a state now and a place I don’t particularly like. And we’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.'

Chema Andres fouled Thiago, fell to the ground and sprang up to confront the Brazilian, who tried to push him away but caught him with a forearm under the jaw.

Igor Thiago's yellow card was upgraded to red after a VAR intervention

Andres collapsed for a second time. When Michael Oliver gave them a yellow card each it seemed fair, but VAR Stuart Attwell sent the referee to the pitch-side screens for a review.

Oliver studied the slow-motion replays and upgraded it to a red card. Off went Thiago, smiling wryly and shaking his head, dismissed for standing his ground and being goaded into a reaction.

He will miss games against Everton, Manchester United and Arsenal.

Opinions of Oliver in the away end did not improve when he gave a penalty for a shirt pull by 5ft 7in Keane Lewis-Potter which somehow sent 6ft 4in Luka Vuskovic somersaulting to the turf.

Vuskovic is already a favourite at the Amex Stadium and it is easy to forget he is only 19. He dominates in the air and reads the game like a seasoned central defender.

And after ten games he is ten points better off than those he left behind at Tottenham.

The Croatia international cannot be looking forward to yet another encounter with England. The two nations meet at Wembley on Thursday. England have put 11 past them in two games this year.
